heroHeadline: Kast Economic Bill Clears Chamber 90-59 as Mapuche Werkén Huenchullán Arrested in Helicopter Operation at Temucuicui
heroSubtitle: Chile's Chamber of Deputies passed the base text of President José Antonio Kast's flagship economic reactivation bill on May 20 (90-59-1), advancing a corporate tax cut from 27% to 23% toward the Senate — though the contested 25-year tax stability clause faces a difficult path. Simultaneously, a joint Army-Carabineros-PDI operation arrested Mapuche community spokesperson Jorge Huenchullán at Temucuicui by helicopter on May 19; the Collipulli court ordered preventive detention on May 20 as prosecutors seek 18 years on drug and weapons charges. The community has denounced a 'racist state structure.' Q1 2026 GDP contracted 0.5% YoY as copper output fell 5.8%, and a Codelco internal audit exposed a 27,000-tonne production overstatement — the state miner's true 2025 output was the lowest since 1998. Kast's approval stands at approximately 26% on Day 70, with 66% of Chileans skeptical the mega reform will revive the economy.
footerNote: Data sourced from official Chilean government records (Biblioteca del Congreso, Banco Central, SERVEL), Rettig and Valech commissions, IACHR, CIPER Chile, and major international outlets.
